content.content:
== Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers asked me to end Rows-For-Another's Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate: eleven years for one holed boat. She gave me a leaf in her own hand to leave in the count-box for the real one, five lockpicks, and 100 gold, the Owing's first price. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the farm.
- Rows-For-Another told me what holds her: her leaf in the count-box inside the estate house, whose key the keeper Hulm-Tei wears; Hulm-Tei's word, which could close the Owing; and Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel north of the bank, who knows the way to her home tree. I'm to break any one of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back where the channel runs on north of the bank. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now, to fetch her back from it. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home, and her Owing will be written onto the keeper. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.

content.content:
Never-Sold: "Three people are held at the heirs' post on the east shore, in the town. The families who hold the Rose, its heirs, hold them. The Rose is the old prison, far to the north, and you are not going there. One of the three can be got out. I want the one held for words, the one we can stand beside in daylight. Tsaxi, the heirs' gate-keeper, stands on the water by the nearest houses, and he will want 300 gold. I will not pay it to loose a stranger I cannot name. If I loose the wrong one, we become the people who loose killers. So find out which is which first, and read whatever proof you can find before you choose. Until you do, the count is whatever Tsaxi says, and he can say the smoke killed one of the three. Not two. Go out of my house and south through the town to the east shore, where the heirs' post stands."

content.content:
Third-Born Tsaxi: "You come from the north house. I know the Broker's children when I see them, and I say that once and no more. I will not explain it. Ask the woman who sent you. A fire went through the upper floors of the Rose. The heirs sent three of their held up to me, to keep until the Rose's leaves came after them. The leaves are the pages that say what each person is held for. I cannot read them, so a reckoner was to carry them and read them out. A reckoner is the one who reads the Rose's leaves and keeps its count. The three are a young man, a young woman and an old woman. The old woman is held for a roof: she owes the heirs for the shelter they gave her. One of the two young ones is held for words said in the yard. The other is held for a killing, and when the leaf is read that one will be put under. To be put under is to be sent down below the Rose, past the gate, where the dead still walk. Nobody comes up. Which of the two young ones is which, I do not know. Both say they are the one held for words. Both can say the words. I was given them at this post, and I did not count what their hands had done. Hear what I can do. I can lose one of the three to the smoke, and the heirs will believe it, because people die in fires. I cannot lose two. Two is a hunt, and the hunt ends at my neck. So only one can leave this post, and it is for you to say which. The reckoner came north by the wet road round the west of the lake. He had four with him, and none came back. His camp is the hut in the swamp, far west of the town, round the lake by the wet road. I do not say what is in that swamp. I say five men went into it and none came back, so go armed or do not go. If you find his leaves, read them before you choose. I cannot, and no one here can."
Objective completed: Speak to Third-Born Tsaxi, keeper of the heirs' post on Blackrose's east shore.
Journal entry (One Out of the Smoke): Tsaxi can count one of the three lost to the Rose's fire, and no more. Walks-Far and Mends-Nets each claim to be held for words; one killed a man. The leaves that say which are with the Rose's reckoner, lost in the western swamp. I'm to learn who is who, and read the leaves if I find them.
New objective: Learn which of the two killed: bring back the reckoner's leaves from his camp in the western swamp, or win the truth from Seven-Floods. Or pay Tsaxi to count one lost without knowing which.
Topics:
  1. Here is the gold you want. Count one lost to the smoke. (300 gold)
  2. Count one of them lost to the smoke. (Persuade)
  3. How did the dead man die?
  4. Who are you?

I was old and coughing, and I owed more than I could ever work off, and that third winter was one more to die inside. She took him at the wash-pool with a net. He did not come out. If those leaves reach the Rose, she is put under, down where nobody comes up. You have read that too. Take her anyway. Take her before me. I am an old woman with smoke in my chest, and I will be dead soon wherever I am. She is young, and she did it for me. Do not mistake me. I want to die near my Hist, and I would give much to lie under it at the end. I will not buy it with her."

content.content:
Never-Sold: "Ussa-Rekh, the Broker, bought hundreds of people out of their Owings on Soulrest's dock, on the shore a short way east of Lilmoth, and now he hires them out, and each freed person's carved token stays in his chest until they have worked a season for him. Heavy-Rope's crew have worked theirs and one more, and I want their tokens in their hands. There is also a bound book on his shelf with my name on it, and I want that too. A person has it back when they have worked a season's hire for him. My crew worked theirs and another. The tokens are still in the chest. Feldril Nethri, a Dunmer who says he works off his own months, keeps about outside the north door, which is locked. He might leave it unbarred for coin or a good word. A season is paid for by Ra'Jhan, the Khajiit berth-master, who keeps the shore at the landward end of the dock. He pays when it is sailed. Without him there is no season. The old man says the hire is promised to the price of eleven people held at Thorn, where it is worst. Hear my side. A last season that becomes two is an Owing with a new name, and we were promised an ending. If the old man wins, my crew row again and I do not know where it stops. Hear his. If we win, the eleven stay at Thorn. I will not tell you he is a bad man. He freed me. Lift the key or talk the door open, or go to Ra'Jhan. Whatever you do in that house, the old man is in the room, and if he sees you, you are a thief."
